task.description:
Combined WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0198. The issue text is in docs/issues/ISS-0198.yaml (artifacts_in) -- read it there; it is deliberately not restated here, which is itself the subject of this issue.

Step 0.5: scan docs/issues/*.yaml for a prior entry with the same root cause (handoff/dispatch size, pipeline latency, doc verbosity). Cite any match. If the same root cause has recurred, raise severity to at least MAJOR.

Step 1: diagnose. Do NOT write the fix -- DOC-UPDATER does that next.

Re-derive, do not inherit: the issue quotes seven task.description lengths from WF03-ISS0117-20260821. Measure them yourself from that run's handoff files and report what you actually get, including any file the seven-number list omits. Then extend the measurement across at least two other recent runs, so a fix is not tuned to one run.

The diagnosis must answer, with evidence rather than preference:
1. Which ONE of the three affected docs is canonical for this rule, and why the other two only point at it.
2. Which counterweight the measurement supports -- stated target length, required structure, cite-a-prior-handoff-by-path, per-run measurement, or a combination. ISS-0198 leaves this open on purpose; close it on evidence.
3. What AC4's measurable check should be, expressed mechanically enough that ISS-0191's linter could implement it without judgement.
4. Whether WF-03 Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER design artefact) and Step 4 (regression test) are structurally applicable to a prose amendment. Recommend SKIP-with-stated-reason or not. Precedent: WF03-ISS0117-20260821 skipped both.

Binding constraint from the issue: do not weaken weak-model tolerance, and do not weaken HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 2's rule that requirement text travels inside the handoff. The target is redundancy with artefacts the handoff already names -- not the explicitness the weak-model constraint requires.

Write the diagnosis into result.summary. next_action: route to DOC-UPDATER.
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5 recorded: docs/issues/ was scanned, and any prior entry with the same root cause is cited by id (or their absence stated)
The WF03-ISS0117-20260821 task.description lengths are re-derived first-hand and quoted, with any discrepancy against the issue's seven figures named explicitly
The measurement is extended to at least two other runs, with per-run figures quoted
Exactly one canonical document is named for the rule, with the reason the other two only point at it
A specific counterweight is recommended and justified from the measurement, not from preference
A mechanically checkable definition for AC4 is proposed, implementable by a linter without judgement
An explicit applicable/SKIP recommendation is given for WF-03 Step 2 and Step 4, each with a reason
No fix is implemented -- no file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS — ISS-0198. Method: this is a process defect, so "reproduce it" means measure it. Every figure below was computed first-hand from handoffs/*/*.json by script (json.load + len on task.description, os.path.getsize, completed_at minus started_at), not read from the issue or from any prior handoff.

=== STEP 0.5 — REGISTRY LOOKUP ===
docs/issues/ contains 123 entries; all were scanned (grep over the full set for latency / wall-clock / verbosity / dispatch / handoff-size / context-window terms, then each hit read).
NO PRIOR ENTRY HAS THIS ROOT CAUSE. There is no resolved issue about dispatch size, handoff verbosity, or pipeline latency. This is therefore NOT a recurrence, and WF-03 Step 0.5's "raise to at least MAJOR on recurrence" does NOT fire. Severity stays MINOR.
Three adjacent-but-distinct entries, cited because they bear on the fix:
- ISS-0021 (resolved) — a doc contradiction spanning the SAME three files as ISS-0198 (core-directives.md / HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md / ORCHESTRATOR.md). Not the same root cause, but it is the governing PRECEDENT for question 1: it was resolved by naming one owner rather than by editing all three, and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 still carries its note recording that three documents disagreeing cost two agents a stop-and-flag each before anyone fixed the source.
- ISS-0191 (OPEN, not built) — the handoff linter. AC4's check can only be a SPEC handed to ISS-0191, not a running check. ISS-0191 also names ISS-0190 (the 15+13 existing schema violations) as a likely prerequisite, so a size check added to the linter's scope will not run green until ISS-0190 is cleared. This is a sequencing constraint on any fix that claims AC4 is "enforced".
- ISS-0196 (open) — commit the handoff at dispatch. Adjacent, different root cause. Confirmed live during this step: `git status --porcelain` showed handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/ UNTRACKED at the moment this agent claimed it, i.e. ISS-0196's exact symptom reproduced again on this very run. Filed below as a MINOR issue rather than absorbed.

=== RE-DERIVED: WF03-ISS0117-20260821 ===
The issue states "nine handoff files ... 1,405 / 4,867 / 10,027 / 6,780 / 10,281 / 6,290 / 9,115 characters ... producing handoff files of 21-29 KB each." Measured directly, THREE OF THOSE CLAIMS ARE WRONG:

file                            desc      file size
step-005-registry-lookup         1,405      8,693
step-01-diagnose                 4,867     37,358
step-03-amendment               10,027     32,565
step-03b-reviewer-gate           6,780     39,469
step-03c-rework1                10,281     25,996
step-03d-reviewer-regate         6,290     41,723
step-03e-ridealong               8,915     28,974   <-- issue says 9,115
step-03f-reviewer-final          7,300     28,749   <-- omitted by the issue
step-03g-rework2                 6,046     22,030   <-- omitted by the issue
step-03h-reviewer-close          6,437     30,000   <-- omitted by the issue

DISCREPANCY 1 — file count. The run has TEN handoff files, not nine. The issue's own seven-number list covers only files 1-7 and silently stops at step-03e; the three REVIEWER/DOC-UPDATER files that closed the run are absent.
DISCREPANCY 2 — the seventh figure. step-03e-ridealong's description is 8,915 characters, not 9,115. Digit transposition; immaterial to the argument, but it is a re-derivable number that was not re-derived.
DISCREPANCY 3 — file size range, and this one IS material. Actual range is 8,693-41,723 bytes, not "21-29 KB". The issue understates the top of the range by ~44%. It matters because it points at the wrong target: within this run, r(task.description, file size) is weak and the largest FILES are not the ones with the largest DESCRIPTIONS. step-03d-reviewer-regate is the biggest file at 41,723 bytes on a 6,290-char description, because its result.summary is 24,369 chars. Across the run, result.summary totals 143,465 chars against task.description's 68,348 — RESULT PROSE IS 2.1x THE DISPATCH PROSE. A fix aimed only at task.description addresses the smaller half of the artefact it is trying to shrink.

=== EXTENDED TO FOUR MORE RUNS (issue required two) ===
run                    steps  desc median/max   min/step median/max  total min
WF03-ISS0117-20260821    10    6,608 / 10,281      7.4 / 12.2          73.2
WF03-ISS0109-20260821    14    5,497 / 12,187      3.4 / 18.3          86.8
WF03-ISS0106-20260821    15    4,825 /  6,909      5.5 / 23.8         137.4
WF02-REQ113-20260821     19      220 /    646      1.5 / 22.0         104.5
WF02-REQ114-20260821     11      291 /    666      2.5 /  5.0          25.4
And corpus-wide over all 584 handoff files (582 parseable; 2 unparseable/task-less, consistent with ISS-0191's finding): desc median 682, p75 1,253, p90 3,191, p95 5,138, max 12,187, mean 1,304.

=== ROOT CAUSE, IN THREE FINDINGS ===

FINDING A — THE ISSUE'S IMPLIED CAUSAL CLAIM IS NOT SUPPORTED. ISS-0198 reads as "long dispatches cause long steps." Measured, they do not. Pooled over the 69 timed steps in the five runs, r(desc chars, step minutes) = 0.281 — dispatch size explains under 8% of latency variance. Within-run it is inconsistent (ISS-0109 r=0.102, ISS-0106 r=0.249, ISS-0117 r=0.609). The counterexamples are direct: ISS-0109's LONGEST dispatch (12,187 chars, CODE-DESIGNER) completed in 2.3 minutes, while its 4,721-char TEST-RUNNER step took 18.3. Conversely WF02-REQ113 dispatched at 63-646 chars throughout and still produced 22.0-, 15.0-, 14.0- and 12.0-minute steps. Step latency tracks whether the step does real work (runs a suite, implements, re-derives evidence) far more than it tracks how much it was told. THIS MATTERS FOR THE FIX: a rule justified as "shorter dispatches make the pipeline faster" would be justified by something the data does not show, and would be the first thing a future agent correctly discards.

FINDING B — SHORTER IS NOT SAFER EITHER; THE HARM IS AT BOTH ENDS. WF02-REQ113, the shortest-dispatch run measured (median 220 chars), needed 3 CODE-DESIGNER attempts, 3 design-validator gates, an ELIXIR-DEV rework, a security regate, a reviewer regate and two reruns — 9 of its 19 files are rework/regate/rerun, and 3 carry a non-PASS result. Its total wall-clock was 104.5 minutes, LONGER than ISS-0117's 73.2, the run that triggered this issue. Meanwhile ISS-0106 (desc median 4,825) and ISS-0109 (median 5,497) recorded 0 and 1 rework respectively with zero non-PASS results. Rework is the dominant latency term and under-specification buys it. A bare "keep it short" rule would move cost from dispatch tokens into rework turns at roughly 7-22 minutes each. This is also exactly what the weak-model constraint predicts, so it is corroboration, not a surprise.

FINDING C — THE ACTUAL MECHANISM IS CITE-AND-ALSO-RESTATE, AND IT IS MEASURABLE WITH NO JUDGEMENT. Dispatch lengths are not a continuum, they are BIMODAL. Among the 66 handoffs in the five runs that carry a non-empty artifacts_in: 34 have a description over 1,500 chars that ALSO names one of its own artifacts_in files by basename (median length 5,497), and the other 32 have a median of 322. There is almost nothing in between. Corpus-wide the overlap is total: of 582 measured files, 20 have a description over 6,000 chars, and ALL 20 OF THEM name an artifacts_in basename inside that description. Not one long dispatch is long for any other reason.
The pattern is visible verbatim. WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json (12,187 chars, the corpus maximum) opens: "READ FIRST, in this order: handoffs/.../step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json (the diagnosis -- read result.summary in full)" and then, in the same block, "THE DIAGNOSIS IN ONE PARAGRAPH (authoritative...". It routes the agent to the artefact AND restates the artefact. Both halves are individually defensible; together they are pure duplication, and it is the duplicated half that ISS-0198's binding constraint identifies as the legitimate target.
WHY NOTHING STOPS IT: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 provides exactly one structured slot for "text copied verbatim from a named source" — context.requirement_text — and scopes it to docs/requirements.yaml entries only. Measured: requirement_text is the empty object in 66 of the 69 handoffs in these five runs (the 3 exceptions are WF-02 Step 00/Final files). So in every WF-03 run measured, the schema's copied-source field sits empty while 4,867-12,187 chars of copied source text is carried in task.description, a free-prose field with no stated shape. The rule pushing toward explicitness has a structured outlet; the content it produces has none, so it lands in prose, where nothing can measure it. That is the root cause.
SCOPE CORRECTION: this is a RECENT drift, not a standing property. 36 of the 45 corpus files over 4,000 chars (80%) belong to five runs all dated 2026-08-21; the corpus median is 682. The pipeline did not always do this.

=== Q1 — CANONICAL DOCUMENT: docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md ===
The rule belongs in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2, adjacent to the context.requirement_text paragraph, for four reasons that are structural rather than aesthetic:
1. IT IS A FIELD-SEMANTICS RULE. Per Finding C the defect is that task.description absorbs content belonging in a structured slot. Section 2 is the section that defines what each field means and already carries the only precedent — the requirement_text paragraph, which states the writer (ORCH), the readers, and that naming a file in artifacts_in is not a substitute. The new rule is the mirror of that one and is unreadable apart from it.
2. AUDIENCE — this is decisive. ORCHESTRATOR.md is read by ORCH alone. A size rule living there could be written by ORCH and checked by nobody, which violates core-directives' "Every producing step has a validating step" — the project's stated central redundancy principle. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md is read by every role, so a rule stated there can be enforced by the receiving agent and reported as a MINOR issue in its result.issues, exactly the mechanism section 1.1 and the Instruction Precedence section already establish for malformed handoffs.
3. PRECEDENCE. core-directives.md is rank 5 and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md is rank 4 under Instruction Precedence, first match wins. The weak-model explicitness constraint lives in core-directives. Putting the counterweight in the SAME file makes two rank-5 rules that pull opposite ways with no tie-break — the precedence chain cannot resolve an intra-file conflict. At rank 4, the counterweight scopes the rank-5 rule cleanly, and it stays overridable per-dispatch by the rank-1 task block, which is the right escape hatch for a genuinely unusual step.
4. ENFORCEMENT ANCHOR. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's closing Enforcement note is where ISS-0191's linter is specified. AC4's mechanical check has to live where the linter's spec lives or it will not be implemented.
WHY THE OTHER TWO ONLY POINT AT IT — and the pattern to copy is already in the tree: ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10 opens "This section is the canonical definition of the direct-action exception. Other files point here; none of them restates the test." Use that wording shape verbatim.
- core-directives.md: one sentence appended to "Load Scoped Context, Not Whole Files" noting that the same anti-duplication principle governs what a handoff restates from its own artifacts_in, pointing to HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2. That section is the natural host because it already contains the identical argument ("Naming the file in artifacts_in is not sufficient") applied to the reader; the new rule applies it to the writer. It must NOT restate the threshold — a duplicated threshold is ISS-0021 recurring in the same three files.
- ORCHESTRATOR.md: one line in section 6 or beside section 7, stating that ORCH authors task blocks under HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's structure rule, pointing there. No restatement.
Note the self-consistency requirement: a fix for a redundancy defect that writes the rule into three files is the defect.

=== Q2 — COUNTERWEIGHT: REQUIRED STRUCTURE + CITE-BY-PATH, WITH PER-RUN MEASUREMENT. EXPLICITLY NOT A TARGET LENGTH. ===
Rejected on evidence, not preference:
- STATED TARGET LENGTH, as the primary lever — REJECTED. Finding A shows length does not predict latency (r=0.281), so the stated benefit would not materialise; Finding B shows the shortest-dispatch run had the highest rework and a LONGER total wall-clock than the run that prompted the issue. A length target optimises a variable that is not the cost driver, and pressures agents toward the failure mode that is.
- CITE-A-PRIOR-HANDOFF-BY-PATH, alone — INSUFFICIENT. Finding C shows agents ALREADY cite by path; all 20 corpus files over 6,000 chars name their artifacts_in. Adding "cite by path" changes nothing, because the defect is the restatement that accompanies the citation, not a missing citation.
- REQUIRED STRUCTURE — SUPPORTED, and it is the only option addressing the measured mechanism. The rule should be: when task.description reproduces content from a file already listed in artifacts_in, it cites that path AND states what the receiving agent must do with it, and does not reproduce it. Where copied source text genuinely must travel inside the handoff (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's rule, which stays intact), it travels in a STRUCTURED context field keyed by source path — generalising context.requirement_text beyond docs/requirements.yaml — never in task.description prose. This preserves section 2's guarantee that the receiving agent need not open a large file, preserves weak-model explicitness in full (nothing becomes less explicit; the same text moves to a labelled slot), and removes only the duplication that ISS-0198's binding constraint names as the target. It also fixes the deeper problem that today the copy is unmeasurable because it is unlabelled.
- PER-RUN MEASUREMENT — SUPPORTED as the enforcement half, not the rule itself. It is nearly free and is the only mechanism that will notice the drift recurring, given Finding C shows it appeared inside a single day.
The combination is the recommendation. Structure is the rule; measurement is the check; length is a symptom that the measurement reports and no rule targets directly.
SECOND-ORDER NOTE FOR THE DESIGNER, from Discrepancy 3: result.summary is 2.1x task.description in the run under study, and this diagnosis is itself a long result.summary. Whatever structure rule is written for the dispatch side should be written so it can be extended to result.summary later; recommend the fix stay silent on result.summary rather than pre-deciding it, and that a separate issue be filed. Silently extending a dispatch rule to results would exceed this issue's scope.

=== Q3 — AC4'S MECHANICAL CHECK (spec for ISS-0191's linter) ===
Per handoff file, using only json.load, len, str.find and os.path.basename — no judgement, no NLP:
  desc  = task.description or ""
  ain   = context.artifacts_in or []
  names = { basename(p) for p in ain }
CHECK H-SIZE-1 (WARN) "cite-and-restate": len(desc) > 6000 AND any(n in desc for n in names).
  Threshold justification, not preference: corpus p90 = 3,191 and p95 = 5,138, so 6,000 sits above p95 and flags 20 of 582 files (3.4%) — the tail, not the norm. In the five runs studied it flags 12 of 69 (17%). Both conditions are literal substring/length tests. Every one of the 20 corpus files it flags is a true positive under Finding C.
CHECK H-SIZE-2 (WARN) "under-specified": len(desc) + sum(len(ac) for ac in task.acceptance_criteria) < 400. Flags 9 of 69 (13%) in the studied runs, catching WF02-REQ113's under-specified dispatches. Present so the fix cannot be satisfied by truncation — Finding B's failure mode.
CHECK H-SIZE-3 (INFO, per run, never fails): emit n_steps, median/max/total len(task.description), and the count of H-SIZE-1 hits. This is the per-run measurement of Q2; it is a report, not a gate.
Both WARN checks are advisory by design: neither condition proves a defect on its own, and turning either into a hard failure would let a passing linter be bought by deleting text, which core-directives' "Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures" forbids. All three are computable from the file alone with no repo state and no cross-file reads.
SEQUENCING (from Step 0.5): ISS-0191 is open and unbuilt, and names ISS-0190 as a likely prerequisite. AC4 can be satisfied only by SPECIFYING these checks in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's Enforcement note and adding them to ISS-0191's scope. Any wording implying the check RUNS today would be false.

=== Q4 — WF-03 STEPS 2 AND 4 ===
STEP 2 (CODE-DESIGNER design artefact) — SKIP. Reason: the deliverable is a prose amendment to three documentation files plus a scope addition to an open issue. lib/letflow/design/ artefacts specify interfaces, @specs, schema and state shapes; there is no module, function, or data shape here, so the artefact would have no content of its own kind and would restate the amendment — the very duplication this issue exists to remove. Precedent: WF03-ISS0117-20260821, an amendment to two of these same three files, skipped Step 2. Routing note: DOC-UPDATER is the correct producer, gated by REVIEWER, which is the shape ISS-0117 actually used.
STEP 4 (regression test) — SKIP, with the reason stated in the handoff. A regression test for this fix would have to assert a property over handoffs/*.json, and ISS-0191 records that ZERO ExUnit tests assert anything over handoffs/*.json today (6 grep hits, all provenance comments). Writing a partial linter as this run's regression test is precisely what ISS-0117 declined to do, and ISS-0191 records that decision and its reasoning. Building the real check belongs to ISS-0191, whose own prerequisite (ISS-0190's 15+13 existing violations) is not cleared — a check added now would be red on arrival for reasons unrelated to this fix. The correct discharge is to add H-SIZE-1/2/3 to ISS-0191's scope and record here that Step 4 is deferred to it, NOT to claim the fix is mechanically enforced.
Both SKIPs must be written into their handoffs with these reasons, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's SKIPPED definition ("state why in summary").

=== BINDING CONSTRAINTS — HELD ===
Weak-model tolerance: not weakened. Nothing above makes any instruction less explicit; the structure rule relocates copied text into a labelled field and leaves instruction text alone. H-SIZE-2 exists specifically to prevent a fix that trades explicitness for brevity.
HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's rule that requirement text travels inside the handoff: not weakened; generalised. The recommendation extends the copy-it-inline guarantee from docs/requirements.yaml to any cited source, and keeps the existing prohibition on substituting an artifacts_in entry for the text.

=== SELF-MEASUREMENT ===
This dispatch: task.description 1,999 chars, acceptance_criteria 842, artifacts_in 6. Under H-SIZE-1 it does not flag (1,999 < 6,000); under H-SIZE-2 it does not flag (2,841 > 400). It sits between the two modes Finding C identifies, which is the behaviour the recommended rule is meant to produce.

=== WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE ===
1. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 — add the structure rule beside context.requirement_text, phrased as canonical ("other files point here; none restates it", per ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10's wording), generalising the structured copied-source slot beyond docs/requirements.yaml.
2. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md Enforcement note — add H-SIZE-1/2/3 as specified checks.
3. core-directives.md "Load Scoped Context, Not Whole Files" — one pointer sentence, no threshold, no restatement.
4. ORCHESTRATOR.md — one pointer line, no restatement.
5. docs/issues/ISS-0191.yaml — add H-SIZE-1/2/3 to scope; note ISS-0190 sequencing.
6. Do NOT state a target length as a rule anywhere. Finding A does not support it and Finding B argues against it.

NO FIX WAS IMPLEMENTED. No file outside handoffs/ was modified by this step (git status --porcelain confirms the only working-tree changes are handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json, and this run's own directory).

issues.description: ISS-0198's own measured figures are partly wrong and were re-derived here: the run has TEN handoff files not nine (step-03f/03g/03h omitted from its seven-number list); step-03e is 8,915 chars not 9,115; and the stated 21-29 KB file-size range is actually 8,693-41,723 bytes. The third error is material -- it points the fix at task.description when result.summary is 2.1x larger (143,465 vs 68,348 chars across that run). The issue record should be corrected so a later reader does not inherit the wrong numbers.

ISS-0198's implied causal claim (long dispatches cause long steps) is NOT supported by measurement: pooled r(desc chars, step minutes) = 0.281 over 69 timed steps, and WF02-REQ113 with 63-646-char dispatches still produced 22.0/15.0/14.0/12.0-minute steps and a LONGER total wall-clock (104.5 min) than the run that prompted the issue (73.2 min). Any fix justified on latency grounds would rest on a false premise. The defensible justification is redundancy elimination, which is what the issue's own binding constraint already names.

ISS-0196 reproduced live on this run: handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/ was UNTRACKED in git at the moment this agent claimed its handoff, so the dispatched task text existed only in the dispatching session. Recorded as fresh evidence for ISS-0196 rather than absorbed.
2 of the 584 handoff JSON files under handoffs/ are unparseable or carry no task block, independently reproducing part of ISS-0191/ISS-0190's finding while measuring this issue.

result.next_action: Route to DOC-UPDATER for the prose amendment (WF-03 Step 2 recommended SKIP -- no design artefact applies to a prose amendment; precedent WF03-ISS0117-20260821), gated by REVIEWER. Canonical target is docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2 plus its Enforcement note; core-directives.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md take pointer-only edits with no restated threshold. Step 4 recommended SKIP, deferred to ISS-0191 with H-SIZE-1/2/3 added to its scope.
